guide.title: Hematologic Emergencies
guide.lead: Blood disorders turn small problems into big ones. A sickle cell patient in pain needs analgesia fast. An anticoagulated patient with a bump on the head needs a scan. Severe sickle cell, chest symptoms and fever can kill quickly.

groups.title: Pain crisis
items: Severe bone, chest or abdominal pain
Keep warm; fluids; oxygen if SpO₂ below 94%

groups.title: Can kill
items: Acute chest syndrome: chest pain, fever, cough, hypoxia
Stroke (children), splenic sequestration (pale, big spleen, shock)
Fever: no working spleen, overwhelming infection

sections.title: Bleeding risk
rows: Any head injury: hospital; CT within 8 hours even if well
Joint and muscle bleeds, head injury
Bring their factor and treatment card
Fever, rash, wheeze, low BP during a transfusion
Stop it, keep the line, oxygen, keep the bag

sections.title: Clots and anemia
items: DVT: one swollen, warm, painful leg; don't massage it
Severe anemia: pale, tired, breathless, fast pulse, chest pain

quiz.q: A 16-year-old with sickle cell disease has severe limb pain, temperature 37.9 °C, SpO₂ 94%. Priority?
options: Prompt analgesia, keep warm, fluids, gentle handling and transport
Wait for the pain to settle
quiz.explanation: Cold promotes sickling; oxygen if SpO₂ falls below 94%.

quiz.q: A 75-year-old on warfarin hit his head; small cut, now well. Plan?
options: Neuro assessment and transport for CT
Vitamin K and observe at home
quiz.explanation: Anticoagulated head injuries need a scan within 8 hours even if well.

quiz.q: Chest pain, fever, cough and hypoxia in sickle cell disease:
options: Acute chest syndrome: a leading cause of death

quiz.q: A trigger for a sickle cell crisis:
quiz.explanation: Also infection, dehydration, hypoxia, stress, altitude.

quiz.q: Fever in a child with sickle cell disease is dangerous because:
A suspected transfusion reaction. First action?
quiz.explanation: Keep the line with new tubing; keep the bag.

quiz.q: One swollen, warm, painful calf. Avoid:
quiz.explanation: Could dislodge clot to the lungs.

quiz.q: A hemophilia patient hits his head and feels fine. Plan?
options: Emergency transport with his factor and treatment card

quiz.q: A pale child with sickle cell disease, big spleen and shock:

flashcards.question: Severe anemia
flashcards.answer: Pallor, fatigue, breathlessness on exertion, dizziness, tachycardia, chest pain.

flashcards.question: Acute chest syndrome
flashcards.answer: Chest pain, fever, cough, breathlessness, hypoxia in sickle cell disease; a leading cause of death.

flashcards.question: Sickle cell crisis triggers
flashcards.answer: Infection, dehydration, cold, hypoxia, stress, altitude.

flashcards.question: Anticoagulants and head injury
flashcards.answer: Bleeding risk is high and signs can be delayed: hospital assessment and CT within 8 hours even if well.

flashcards.question: Deep vein thrombosis
flashcards.answer: One swollen, warm, red, painful leg. Don't massage it; it can cause PE.

flashcards.question: Transfusion reaction
flashcards.answer: Stop the transfusion, keep the line with new tubing, oxygen, monitor, keep the bag.

flashcards.question: Hemophilia and head injury
flashcards.answer: Missing clotting factor: even minor head trauma can bleed. Emergency transport with their factor and card.

flashcards.question: Sickle cell pain: EMS care
flashcards.answer: Prompt analgesia (within 30 minutes of arrival), warmth, fluids, oxygen if SpO₂ below 94%, gentle handling.

critical.scenario: A 22-year-old with sickle cell disease has worsening chest pain, cough and breathlessness for 12 hours after a cold; vomiting for 2 days. SpO₂ 90%, temperature 38.8 °C, HR 114.
critical.question: Diagnosis and management?

options.t: Acute chest syndrome: oxygen, analgesia, sit up, keep warm, rapid transport with pre-alert
Simple pain crisis: 2 L/min and routine transport
options.f: Hypoxia, fever and chest symptoms are acute chest syndrome.

critical.explanation: Hypoxia drives more sickling; these patients may need exchange transfusion.
critical.kpi: Differentiates acute chest syndrome from simple vaso-occlusive crisis in sickle cell disease

critical.scenario: A 70-year-old on apixaban fell down three stairs and hit his head. GCS 15, no symptoms, small bruise. He wants to stay home.
critical.question: How do you manage this?

options.t: Explain the delayed bleeding risk, recommend transport for CT; if he still refuses, involve medical direction and document carefully
Accept the refusal: he looks fine

options.f: A capable adult can refuse; inform and document.

options.t: Tell him to stop the apixaban

critical.explanation: Anticoagulated head injuries need a CT within 8 hours even if well.
critical.kpi: Recognizes the danger of seemingly minor head trauma in anticoagulated patients

critical.scenario: The day after hip replacement: sudden breathlessness and left chest pain. HR 118, RR 28, SpO₂ 88%. The left leg is swollen, warm and red.
critical.question: Likely sequence and management?

options.t: DVT that has caused a pulmonary embolism: oxygen, sit up, don't massage the leg, rapid transport
Massage the leg to improve flow

critical.explanation: Massive PE can cause collapse: be ready for arrest.
critical.kpi: Recognizes the progression from DVT to pulmonary embolism with characteristic findings
